parameters.errorMessage: Retention purge did not fully verify. The audit_log row for this run was written FIRST, so the shortfall is already on the compliance record before this stop: it carries requested / deleted / unaccounted and names every storage_path still sitting in the kyc-documents bucket. purged_at was written ONLY for the objects Supabase confirmed it deleted; every unaccounted row is deliberately left unmarked so Find Expired Documents selects it again on the next run. Absence from Supabase Storage's bulk-delete response means NOT DELETED - it never means fine. This stop exists so the execution shows red and reaches the error workflow; it does not undo anything and it does not suppress the audit row.

nodes.name: Reconcile Storage Deletions
nodes.notes: Matches the Storage bulk-delete response against the requested paths and emits ONE item: requested / deleted / unaccounted / confirmed_ids. Absence from the response means NOT DELETED. Also collapses the array-split fan-out that let the old graph mark all 500 ids before the failure branch ran.

nodes.name: Anything Confirmed Deleted?
nodes.notes: TRUE = at least one object was confirmed gone, so Mark Rows Purged may write purged_at for exactly those ids. FALSE = nothing confirmed, so the PATCH is skipped entirely (id=in.() would be a malformed PostgREST filter) and the run goes straight to the audit row. Both outputs converge on Summarise Purge -- the audit row is written either way.

nodes.name: Purge Verdict Clean?
nodes.notes: Runs AFTER Log Purge to Audit on purpose: the compliance row is on the record before the run is allowed to go red. TRUE = delivery.status SUCCESS, nothing more to do. FALSE = PARTIAL or FAILED, so escalate through the stopAndError into errorWorkflow iYJkh1kztWxZXDbT.
